blocks.text: Dry kick, then dribbling low toms: accelerate, stumble, recover. Overdriven bass holds a stubborn groove; late snare, scratchy guitar chops, one sour piano chord.
Full-bodied, smoky, conversational; restrained power. Bass and kick carry the pulse.

We built tall walls from tape
Hung law in a gold frame
Stamped “process” on thin gates
Called stall by a new name
Snare sharpens; toms trip between phrases. Guitar answers in dirty scratches.

Soft and slow
Rooms hum low
Lights snap on
It’s all for show
Bass thickens, guitar chops harder. Vocal rises into chest voice; let “drown” fray.

Speed dressed up as law
Gave fear a crown
Quick hands rule
Slow truths drown
Voice exposed and unwavering; leave space between couplets.

When doctrine slips
And motives show

What holds the weight?
We don’t know
Raw garage-soul groove, drums slipping around a steady bass. Open up the vocal on “clarity.”

If mercy swings
That wrecking ball
It’s not the end
Just stresses the walls

The beams all shake
So do we
That’s not doom
That’s clarity
Bass stays steady; low toms bounce faster, lose the downbeat, then recover. Snare snaps back; rough guitar chord. No solo.
Dirty bass and clipped guitar. Vocal punches each phrase, alternating near-speech with bursts of melody.

Work lost heat
Cash left town
Goods float free
No roots in ground

Charts glow blue
Lines climb fast
Jobs drop out
But “growth” holds fast
Muted guitar, bare bass, displaced snare, one sour piano strike. Vocal low and accusatory.

Work’s a ghost
A judge we’d host
Now judgment’s wide
We stand exposed
Isolated bass notes and soft kick; close-miked voice with audible breath. No melodrama.

Plenty’s not kind
It strips things bare
When lack is gone
You see what’s there
Toms tumble into gaps; snare lands early, late, or not at all. Bass holds firm. Vocal plants every word against the shifting beat.

Quakes don’t make
They break release

Fires don’t start
They free the heat
Raw sustained belt on “burns.” Full-band stop.
Bass returns alone; dribbling toms stagger and lock in. Jagged guitar joins. Bigger, never cleaner.
Hardest groove. Huge, gritty, soulful female vocal; conviction over polish. Ragged guitar chords and tumbling drums.

When doctrine slips
And speed takes throne
We feel the crack
Down to bone

If sure things fall
Let them fall
Mercy might
Break us all
“Break us all” opens into an aching, unpolished belt.

The beams all shake
So do we
That’s not weak
That’s clarity
Hold “clarity” until the note frays; abruptly release.
Guitar, then bass disappear. Drums turn unnaturally precise. One dry piano note. Vocal nearly spoken.

Time to choose
What we become

notebook.style: Raw, sweaty dance-punk and garage-soul with an elastic funk pulse, Midtempo, live, imperfect, confrontational, Dry, heavy kick and snare; low toms dribble, accelerate, miss a step, and recover while bass holds the floor, Thick, overdriven electric bass plays a stubborn, danceable riff, Scratchy distorted guitar chops against the beat, opening into ragged power chords at peaks, Occasional sour piano strikes, never jaunty; no horns, Commanding female lead: huge chest resonance, smoky grain, sharp diction, soulful bends, and fierce conviction behind every word, Lower, intimate verses rise into raw, full-throated belts on pivotal lines, never polished pop runs or constant shouting, Rhythmic gaps and sudden band dropouts create tension, not a cinematic crescendo, Final refrain hits hardest; outro strips to exposed speech and silence, Gritty room ambience, little reverb, audible human edges, No choir, synth gloss, theatrical delivery, or cabaret swing
